Claims and Deductions process	- Use Case brief
Some of the reasons for Deductions are (industry standard practice in the CPG sector):
- Trade Related
- Claiming a rebate believed to be due by way of an off invoice promotion
- Deducting due to issues with on invoice promotions
- Logistics Related
- Deducting from a remittance due to quality issues with a shipment
- Deducting from a remittance due to shipment shortages
- Deducting from a remittance due to pricing errors. [Anonymized Customer] are encouraged to claim rebates by the agreed process, i.e., enter a claim to be assessed and, if valid, set off against future invoices or receive a rebate payment – all via a credit memo process. However, it is common practice for [Anonymized Customer] to deduct directly against sales invoices, so that they will short pay against and invoice or a group of invoices. These deductions are either against specific invoices (detailed on remittance) or not related to a specific invoice (bulk deductions). This has spread across all industries, and deductions are a common practice not only for collecting promotions, but also for any kind of dispute or misunderstanding, whether it's a pricing error, transportation related, damages, and so on. This is also the hardest challenge for the receivables departments to resolve because of the need for approval from outside receivables, like sales or shipping. The [Anonymized Customer] may short pay based on their own policies and procedures. It's up to you to resolve these claims. According to market surveys, deductions can represent 5 to 15 percentage of revenue, depending on the industry. Of that number, 5.1 to 10 percent are invalid or unauthorized. In some industries it can be a lot higher.
